run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T14:35:47Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is driven by frontend-proxy's own ingress spans on the frontend route returning HTTP 504 after about 15 s. Over the window the ingress operation carried 236.4 error spans against 23,687 non-error spans, and from about 14:37 errors ran at 42-117 spans per 5 minutes, with the 5-minute rate peaking at 0.389 error spans/s at 14:44:47 - the same magnitude as the alert annotation's 0.39999. A full trace (e1149d121221112b45608659f572e755) shows the mechanism: frontend-proxy ingress 504 after 15.094 s and its visible child 'router frontend egress' ending at 15.061 s with error="true" and http.status_code "0", while frontend's own POST /api/checkout span ran 17.595 s and still returned 200, with the time spent in frontend -> checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (17.510 s) -> checkout 'orders publish' (17.438 s, the Kafka produce span). In 14:36:26-14:48:26 the only operations exceeding 10 s are exactly that chain (checkout orders publish 284.9 spans, PlaceOrder 288.0, the frontend /api/checkout chain 287-291, frontend-proxy ingress and egress 291.2), whereas in 14:12:00-14:32:00 no frontend, checkout or frontend-proxy span exceeded 10 s. Checkout's 'orders publish' histogram shows about 1,252 spans in 14:10:47-14:47:27, of which about 207 exceeded 15,000 ms and another ~123 fell in 10,000-15,000 ms, and the per-5-minute count of publishes slower than 15 s was 0 in every evaluated window ending 14:35:00 or earlier before rising to 24-116 through 14:48. The deepest object the evidence ties to that onset is the single-replica kafka Deployment: its pod was replaced by a rollout at 14:33:16-14:33:18 (old pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 stopped, new kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 created with an identical pod template), checkout began logging Kafka 'connection refused' to 100.65.62.181:9092 at 14:33:35 and 'circuit breaker is open' failures on topic orders until it re-registered broker #1 at 14:35:01, the replacement broker only logged 'Kafka Server started' at 14:34:53 after an unclean log-dir replay, and the slow publishes and the error spike begin immediately afterwards (alert start 14:35:47). A competing explanation that cannot be excluded is the demo feature flag kafkaQueueProblems, which flagd-config currently sets to "on" (value 100, the only chaos flag enabled) and which is described as overloading the Kafka queue; its activation time could not be verified and no publish slower than 15 s existed before about 14:35, so it remains a live hypothesis. A separate, earlier phase of fast HTTP 503s on the frontend route (about 14:11-14:35, with no frontend span in those traces) is a distinct failure mode whose cause was not established. Affected: frontend-proxy (its own ingress error spans/504s) and checkout (its own error spans and its own Kafka failure/slow-publish evidence). Checked and not showing failures of this cause: frontend (0 error spans, but its spans were slow 17-18 s and returned 200), product-catalog, currency, payment, cart, shipping, quote, email, ad, image-provider, accounting, fraud-detection and recommendation show no 10 s+ spans in 14:36-14:48. Not checked: load-generator internals, valkey-cart, postgresql, otel-collector health beyond the absence of spans.

claims.text: In frontend-proxy the operation 'ingress' returned 236.4 error spans over the window against 23,687 non-error spans, and in 14:38:26-14:48:26 the only error spans cluster-wide were frontend-proxy 'ingress' (157.5) and recommendation '/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' (1.07).

frontend-proxy's error rate rose in two steps: 0.004-0.02 error spans/s between 14:11:47 and about 14:35 (5-minute increases of 1-7 spans), then 42.2, 74.4, 62.9, 108.9, 116.7 and 93.9 error spans per 5 minutes from the windows at 14:37 to 14:47, with the 5-minute rate peaking at 0.38889 spans/s at 14:44:47, matching the alert annotation's 'current: 0.39999999999999997'.

The dominant failure is HTTP 504 on frontend-proxy operation 'ingress': in the sampled frontend-proxy error spans read back, every shown ingress error span is 504 with duration about 15.0 s and its child 'router frontend egress' carries error="true" and http.status_code "0".

Trace e1149d121221112b45608659f572e755 shows the causal shape: load-generator POST 15.097 s -> 504, frontend-proxy ingress 15.094 s -> 504 and its egress 15.061 s, while frontend 'POST /api/checkout' 17.595 s returned http 200 and the time is inside frontend 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 17.564 s, checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 17.510 s and checkout 'orders publish' 17.438 s.

In 14:36:26-14:48:26 the only span operations exceeding 10 s are that checkout-to-Kafka chain: checkout 'orders publish' 284.9, checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 288.0, frontend 'POST' 291.2, 'POST /api/checkout' 288.0, 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' 288.0, 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 287.0, frontend-proxy 'ingress' 291.2 and 'router frontend egress' 291.2; by service the >10 s span counts are frontend 1,154, frontend-proxy 582, checkout 573 and all other services <=3.2.

In the earlier window 14:12:00-14:32:00 no frontend, checkout or frontend-proxy span exceeded 10 s (all 0); only ad 1.04, accounting 3.08 and recommendation 2.05 did, so the 504/timeout mechanism was not present then.

The checkout span 'orders publish' (Kafka produce to topic orders) had about 1,252 spans in 14:10:47-14:47:27, of which ~905 were <=2 ms, ~1,045 <=15,000 ms and about 207 above 15,000 ms, with a further ~123 in the 10,000-15,000 ms range (bucket boundaries taken from the returned le values).

Per-5-minute counts of 'orders publish' spans slower than 15 s were 0 for every evaluated window ending at or before 14:35:00 and then 24.1 (14:36:00), 39.1, 53.3, 68.3, 93.3 (14:40:00), 104.4 (14:42:00), 105.6, 115.6 (14:44:00), 111.1, 105.6, 85.0 and 71.1 (14:48:00), so the >15 s produce stalls begin about 14:35-14:36.

The single-replica kafka Deployment in otel-demo was rolled inside the window: Deployment kafka ScalingReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485 from 0 to 1 at 14:33:16, ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485 SuccessfulCreate of pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97, Killing 'Stopping container kafka' on pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 at 14:33:18 and ReplicaSet kafka-ff7884766 SuccessfulDelete at 14:33:18; the revision-1 and revision-2 ReplicaSet pod templates are identical in image, env, resources and volumes.

checkout's own logs show Kafka failures starting 17-19 s after that pod got its stop signal: 'Failed to connect to broker kafka:9092: dial tcp 100.65.62.181:9092: connect: connection refused' and 'Failed to write message: kafka: Failed to produce message to topic orders: circuit breaker is open' from 14:33:35 through 14:34:58, then 'Connected to broker at kafka:9092 (registered as #1)' at 14:35:01.

The replacement Kafka broker logged a dirty stateful restart: Raft transitions at 14:34:42-14:34:45, 'Unable to read the broker epoch in /tmp/kafka-logs.' at 14:34:50, replay of RegisterBrokerRecord with fenced=true, 'Transition from STARTING to STARTED' and 'Kafka Server started' at 14:34:53, so the only broker was not serving client traffic until after 14:34:53.

After 14:35 the new broker's filtered log shows only internal metadata activity - repeated __cluster_metadata segment rolls roughly every 15 s and snapshot-driven segment deletions between 14:40:00 and 14:42:45 - and no broker-side error or warning line in 14:35-14:42.

The flagd-config ConfigMap (created 14:00:11 by Helm release otel-demo) currently holds demo.flagd.json with kafkaQueueProblems defaultVariant "on" (value 100, state ENABLED, description 'Overloads Kafka queue while simultaneously introducing a consumer side delay leading to a lag spike'), while every other chaos flag in that file is "off".
Consumer-side slow spans also exist: accounting's 'order-consumed' span had about 7.1 spans over 10 s in 14:10:47-14:47:27, of which about 3.1 already fell inside 14:12:00-14:32:00.

The earlier low-rate phase is a different, fast failure: frontend-proxy ingress spans return HTTP 503 in about 0.10-0.39 s with 'router frontend egress' http.status_code "0", and the traces (user_browse_product at 14:31:30, user_get_ads at 14:32:15, user_index at 14:12:03) contain no frontend span at all, so frontend never served those requests.

frontend, checkout and frontend-proxy Deployments are each 1/1 ready with 1 available replica; pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-tsdtv and pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-bh295 have restartCount 0 with containers running since 14:00:13 and 14:00:18, the replacement kafka pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 is Running with 0 restarts, and all five nodes are Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure false.

frontend emitted no error spans in the queried windows (0 per 5 min from 14:15 through 14:47) even while its /api/checkout spans lasted 17.6 s and returned 200, so the 504s arise at frontend-proxy's roughly 15 s upstream limit rather than from a frontend error.

Separate finding not tied to this cause: pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zcxzm has restartCount 2, a kubelet Warning BackOff event 'Back-off restarting failed container fraud-detection' at 14:26:22, and Pulled/Created/Started events with count 3 (last at 14:26:35); fraud-detection shows no error spans and no 10 s+ spans in the queried windows.

Primary hypothesis: replacing the only Kafka broker (Deployment kafka rollout at 14:33:16-14:33:18, old pod stopped 14:33:18, replacement broker only started 14:34:53 after an unclean log-dir replay) disrupted checkout's Kafka producer, so produce calls to topic orders first failed at 14:33:35-14:34:58 and then stalled 15-17 s for a persistent fraction of publishes from about 14:35 onward; that latency pushed /api/checkout past frontend-proxy's roughly 15 s upstream limit and produced the 504s behind the alert.

Competing hypothesis that stays open: the fault-injection flag kafkaQueueProblems, currently "on" (100) in the flagd-config ConfigMap, is what sustains the producer and consumer delay behind the >15 s 'orders publish' spans - including a publish starting 14:43:18 that took 17.438 s while the broker was already up - and behind the accounting 'order-consumed' spans over 10 s seen even in 14:12-14:32; its activation time could not be verified and no publish exceeded 15 s before about 14:35, so the timing is unestablished.

The about 14:11-14:35 HTTP 503 phase on the frontend route is a separate failure mode (fast 503, egress http.status_code "0", no frontend server span in the sampled traces); its origin is not identified - frontend was 1/1 ready with 0 restarts, no error spans, and its logs were unreadable, so an upstream connection refusal/reset or transient frontend unavailability remains possible and untested.

Against attributing the whole alert to the checkout/Kafka path: before about 14:35 frontend, checkout and frontend-proxy had zero spans over 10 s and frontend-proxy had only 1-7 error spans per 5 minutes, so the above-zero error rate in 14:11-14:35 came from the separate 503 mode, not from Kafka produce latency.

Against the kafkaQueueProblems flag explaining the whole window: every 5-minute count of 'orders publish' spans slower than 15 s is 0 up to and including the window ending 14:35:00, so a producer-side queue delay was not in effect during 14:10-14:35 even though the flag reads "on" now.

Rejected: frontend-proxy crashing, restarting or being resource-starved as the cause of the errors. Pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-bh295 is Running and ready with restartCount 0 since 14:00:18, its Deployment is 1/1 available, and the 15.094 s ingress spans coincide with a frontend span that stayed in flight 2.5 s longer and returned 200.

Rejected: node-level resource pressure on the cluster as the cause. All five nodes report Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure false, and the frontend, checkout, frontend-proxy and kafka pods run on i-0caf4b73702b2641e with no evictions and no OOM terminations visible in their container states.

Focus remediation on the Kafka produce path: verify the state and latency of the single kafka broker after the 14:33 rollout, whose log dir was restored from an unclean state ('Unable to read the broker epoch in /tmp/kafka-logs.'), and compare order-publish latency with the broker healthy before changing anything else.

Explicitly confirm or turn off the kafkaQueueProblems flag in flagd-config (currently "on" = 100) and re-measure checkout 'orders publish' latency; this is the cheapest decisive test between the two open hypotheses.

Review why the kafka Deployment was rolled at 14:33:16 although its pod template is identical to revision 1, and review the frontend-proxy upstream limit (about 15 s) against /api/checkout latency, which exceeded it by about 2.6 s, so slow-but-successful checkout requests stop surfacing as proxy 504s.
Investigate the fraud-detection restarts separately (restartCount 2, BackOff at 14:26:22); no evidence ties them to the frontend-proxy error rate.

gaps: No Prometheus rule named RequestErrorRate was returned: list_prometheus_rules returned status no_data both for rule_name RequestErrorRate and for an unfiltered call, so the alert expression, its 'above 0' threshold and its evaluation interval could not be verified.

The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so who or what triggered the kafka Deployment rollout at 14:33:16, and whether or when kafkaQueueProblems was set to "on" in flagd-config, cannot be determined.
The traces_span_metrics query for 13:35:47-14:05:47 returned status no_data, so the state before about 14:10:47 is unknown rather than clean.

frontend container logs returned status no_data (0 lines) for three separate windows including an unfiltered read, flagd's flagd/flagd-ui/init-config streams returned no_data, and the previous kafka pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 no longer exists, so application-level errors from those containers could not be read.

The query for a metric carrying HTTP status code per frontend-proxy request (http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name="frontend-proxy"}) returned no_data, and only traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket exist for that service, so the exact 503-versus-504 split over time and the total 503 count are unknown; the phase split is inferred from sampled traces (that sample was also truncated/incomplete: 45 of 1,510 rows read).

The cause of the about 14:11-14:35 fast HTTP 503s on the frontend route is not established: no frontend span appears in those traces, frontend reported no error spans, and frontend logs were unreadable.

fraud-detection's restart cause is not established: its last termination reason and exit code were not visible (lastState empty in current pod status) and its logs were not read; a log read for accounting returned no_data and no log evidence was obtained for fraud-detection.
The roughly 15 s limit frontend-proxy applies to the frontend route is inferred from span durations only; the proxy's Envoy configuration is baked into its image and could not be read.

Prometheus rule and metric inspections reflect the state at query time (about 14:48-14:53), not the state during the incident window, as the tool notes state; the kafka Deployment/ReplicaSet/pod objects are likewise the cluster's state when queried.
next_steps: Verify Kafka broker health and produce latency for topic orders after the 14:33 rollout, and check the broker's log-dir epoch state ('Unable to read the broker epoch in /tmp/kafka-logs.') before any restart.
Confirm the current value and change time of the kafkaQueueProblems flag in the flagd-config ConfigMap with whoever manages feature flags, then re-measure checkout 'orders publish' latency.
Obtain the RequestErrorRate Prometheus rule definition to confirm the exact expression, threshold and window used by the alert.
Review frontend-proxy's upstream timeout configuration (about 15 s) against observed /api/checkout latency and consider whether the timeout or the checkout Kafka publish path should be adjusted.
Collect frontend application logs (and flagd logs) by another means, since container log reads returned no data, to explain the 14:11-14:35 503 phase.
Investigate the fraud-detection pod restarts independently of this alert.

Pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-bh295 is Running and ready with restartCount 0 since 14:00:18, its Deployment is 1/1 available, and the 15.094 s ingress spans coincide with a frontend span that stayed in flight 2.5 s longer and returned 200.

Rejected: node-level resource pressure on the cluster as the cause. All five nodes report Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure false, and the frontend, checkout, frontend-proxy and kafka pods run on i-0caf4b73702b2641e with no evictions and no OOM terminations visible in their container states.
